2026-11-25.title: Fourth Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: The hymn of God's plan of salvation
2026-11-25.verse: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things.
theo: Paul's great blessing opens the mystery of the whole year: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing… he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.” God's plan is “to gather up all things in him.”

Mary's Magnificat is the Church's song of that plan seen from below: God looks on the lowliness of his servant, scatters the proud, lifts up the lowly, fills the hungry. As the year ends and Annunciation approaches, the Church sings with Mary, the first of the redeemed and the image of the Church herself.
outline: Ask: what are you thankful for as this liturgical year ends?
Point 1 · Chosen before the world began
God's plan in Christ embraces us.
Point 2 · He looked on the lowly
Mary's song reverses the world's values.
Point 3 · The Church sings Mary's song
Mary is the image of the Church.
“The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
live: Pray Mary's song slowly this evening in thanksgiving for the year.
Do one act of respect for someone overlooked.
2026-11-25.prayer: Blessed be God, who chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. With Mary I praise you: you have done great things for me, and holy is your name. Amen.

2026-11-25.question: What great things has God done for me this year?

homily: Dear friends, Paul's great blessing opens the mystery of the whole year: blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, just as he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:3–4).

Mary sings the same joy in her Magnificat: my soul magnifies the Lord, for he has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant. He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and lifted up the lowly (Luke 1:46–52). Mary's song is the Church's song.

As the season of the Dedication of the Church comes to an end, let us thank God with Mary for the blessings of a whole year. This evening, sit together as a family, name five blessings of this year, and pray a rosary of thanksgiving. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sang a song of praise to God. Today thank God for five good things he gave you this year!

intro: Paul's hymn of God's plan and Mary's Magnificat close the year in praise.

sub: God chose us before the foundation of the world.
His plan is to gather all things in Christ.
q: And in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
His mercy is for those who fear him from generation to generation.
points.apply: Thank God for three blessings of this year.

q: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things.
points.apply: Do one act of respect for someone overlooked.

sub: Mary is the first of the redeemed.
The Church is called to her humility and praise.
q: Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people whom he has chosen as his heritage.
For he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant… for the Mighty One has done great things for me.

concl: With Mary we sing: holy is his name.
